examples.name: Mount the group
examples.description: Mount one ToastGroup near the app root; call toast() from anywhere.

examples.name: Success toast
examples.jsx: toast.success('Changes saved', { description: 'Your matter is up to date.' })

examples.name: Loading updated to success
examples.description: Reuse the id to update a loading toast in place when it resolves.
examples.jsx: const id = toast.loading('Uploading...'); await upload(); toast.success('Uploaded', { id });

examples.name: Toast with an action
examples.description: Actions appear when the stack is expanded.
examples.jsx: toast('Event created', { description: 'Monday 9:00 AM', actions: <Button size='xs' appearance='subtle'>Undo</Button> })

antiExamples.name: Multiple groups
antiExamples.reason: Mount exactly one ToastGroup; multiple would each render the shared queue.

antiExamples.name: Critical message in a toast
antiExamples.reason: Toasts are transient - do not use them for critical or blocking messages.
antiExamples.jsx: toast.error('Your session expired - unsaved work will be lost')
